# Skill: roblox-ui-designer

**When to use:** Design and build Roblox game UI (HUD, shop, inventory, menus, popups, loading screens) in Figma, Photoshop or straight in Roblox Studio: proposes fitting UI styles (bubbly cartoon, clean minimal, glass, anime/gacha, sci-fi neon, horror, pixel, cozy pastel, competitive HUD, fantasy, comic meme) with ready color/font/shape tokens, designs mobile-safe layouts, converts PSDs and Figma designs, and generates a validated build script (+ .rbxmx) that creates the ScreenGuis and a StyleSheet theme in Studio. Use whenever someone wants UI, GUI, HUD, menus, buttons, a UI style or theme for a Roblox game, or asks 'zrób UI', 'jaki styl UI', 'przenieś UI z Figmy/Photoshopa do Roblox'.

Skill folder (scripts, assets): https://github.com/G3LO1/gelo/tree/main/plugins/roblox-studio/skills/roblox-ui-designer

## File: SKILL.md

# Roblox UI Designer

Goal: UI that fits the game's style, reads instantly on a phone, works with touch, mouse and gamepad, and ends up in Studio as clean, named, themeable instances the code can hook into. Every route (Figma, Photoshop, Studio) ends in one `ui-spec.json`, which a tested script turns into the real UI, so the result doesn't depend on which tool the designer likes.

Answer in the user's language; instance names, tokens and code stay in English.

## 1. Inputs
- Take the screens from the plan (`PRODUCTION_PLAN.md` UI tasks) or the conversation: which screens, what each must show and do, which are MVP.
- Ask once, with AskUserQuestion, only what is missing: where the UI will be designed (**Studio directly** = recommended default when there is no designer; **Figma**; **Photoshop**), existing art/brand/logo, platforms (phone-first unless told otherwise).
- Read the game's genre, audience and world art style from the plan or the map style; the UI must match them.

## 2. Style direction
Read `references/ui-styles.md`. Pick 2-3 styles that fit genre + audience + world art, recommend one, and present each in a few lines: mood, palette swatches (hex), fonts, shape language, one example game. Let the user choose (AskUserQuestion with the recommended option first).

To show rather than tell, build a style tile for the chosen style (or for each candidate): copy `assets/examples/style-tile-bubbly.json`, swap tokens/fonts/shape values for the style, and build it in Studio (or mock it in Figma when the Figma MCP server is connected, see `references/figma.md`).

## 3. Design the screens
For each screen write down before drawing anything: purpose, elements (with names), states (default, empty, loading, error, locked/owned), how it opens/closes, and which elements code drives (labels, buttons, lists). Then lay it out following `references/studio.md` (safe areas, thumb zones, anchors, scale, aspect constraints, text sizes). Names are the contract with the code: `CoinsLabel`, `BuyButton`, `ItemList`.

## 4. Build through the chosen route
Work in a `ui/` folder in the project: `ui/ui-spec.json`, `ui/images/`, `ui/BuildUi.luau`, `ui/<Name>.rbxmx`. The spec format is in `references/ui-spec.md`.
- **Studio directly**: write `ui-spec.json` yourself (tokens from the chosen style, `motion` for the shared animation numbers, `styles` for states and shared looks, screens as designed). For buttons and item cards start from `assets/examples/components.json`: layered white images (separate glow, glass/base, edge light), 9-slice frames, Default/Focused/Pressed/Disabled styled by state tags; regenerate its layer images with `python3 scripts/make_ui_images.py ui/images` or replace them with the style's own.
- **Figma**: follow `references/figma.md` (Claude reads or builds the file through the Figma MCP server, or a community plugin converts it). Ask before creating or editing files in the user's Figma.
- **Photoshop**: follow `references/photoshop.md`; run `scripts/psd_to_spec.py` on the PSD, then add tokens/styles to the generated spec.

Then for every route:
1. `python3 scripts/spec_to_luau.py ui/ui-spec.json -o ui/BuildUi.luau --images ui/images` (checks structure, token/font/image references, selector syntax such as `:Press` not `:Pressed`, `motion` ranges, and 9-slice SliceCenter against the PNGs). Treat every `warning:` as a bug to fix: they flag layouts that are valid Roblox but render wrong, above all zero-sized elements (constraints only shrink; `SizeConstraint RelativeYY` makes width = X.Scale x parent height, so X.Scale 0 means width 0).
2. If Lune is available: `lune run scripts/validate_ui.luau ui/BuildUi.luau ui/<Name>.rbxmx` checks every property name, type and enum against Roblox's real API database and writes a model file. Fix and repeat until it prints OK. Without Lune, say that this check was skipped; Studio will report the same errors when the script runs.
3. Look at it: `python3 scripts/preview_ui.py ui/ui-spec.json -o ui/preview.html --images ui/images` renders an approximate browser preview of every screen at 1920x1080, a phone (844x390) and a tablet, with the Roblox top bar and phone thumb zones drawn on top. Take screenshots (Playwright: `npx playwright screenshot --viewport-size "844, 390" "file:///.../preview.html?screen=Hud&w=844&h=390" hud-phone.png`, or open the file in a browser) and look at them: overlaps, invisible or tiny elements, text overflow, things under the thumb zones. Fonts and text fitting are approximate; Studio is the final check.
4. Wire the states: copy `assets/UiStates.luau` to shared code and call `UiStates.bind(screenGui, { reducedMotion = ... })` on the client; it turns mouse, touch and gamepad input into the state tags the style rules use, replaces the default gamepad selection box with the glow, and `:open(container)` pops components in one after another.
5. Get it into Studio: with Roblox Studio MCP tools, `list_roblox_studios`, confirm the place, run `BuildUi.luau` with `execute_luau`, then `screen_capture` to look at it (desktop and a phone size in the Device Emulator if possible) and fix what looks wrong. Without MCP: the user runs `BuildUi.luau` in the Command Bar or drags in the `.rbxmx`.

The build script never deletes: a ScreenGui with the same name is kept as `<Name>_Backup` (disabled).

## 5. Check
Go through the checklist at the end of `references/studio.md`. Put the design (or the preview) and the Studio screenshots side by side, screen by screen, and list every difference: text a size off (Roblox measures the line, design tools the letter), lost title spacing, dark bands on stretched frames (9-slice), layers in the wrong order. Check each component's states with mouse (focused, pressed), touch (pressed only) and gamepad (selection, A) in a playtest or the Device Emulator. Don't claim the UI looks right on phones unless a screenshot or emulator check actually happened; list what still needs a human eye.

## 6. Hand-off
- Images to upload (Asset Manager > Bulk Import) and where their IDs go (`images` in the spec, then rebuild); no `rbxassetid://0` may ship. Item/shop icons rendered from 3D models: with a connected Blender MCP server Claude can render them with one camera/light/outline setup for all items (`../roblox-animation-vfx/references/blender.md` section 8); otherwise ViewportFrames in the UI or renders by the team.
- The element names and tags the code should use; offer `roblox-luau-codegen` to write the controllers (UI pattern in its `references/patterns.md`: bind by name, `DataController.OnChanged`, `Net.fire`).
- Tokens live in `ReplicatedStorage.UIStyles.<Name>`: editing them in the Style Editor restyles the game (themes, events).

## File: references/figma.md

# Figma -> Roblox

Roblox Studio does not open Figma files. The design is made in Figma, then either Claude reads it through the Figma MCP server and writes `ui-spec.json`, or a community plugin converts it. Either way the result is checked against `studio.md` (scale, anchors, safe areas). Research sources: Figma Community plugin pages, DevForum threads (2023-2026), Roblox Creator Hub.

## Contents
1. Setting up the Figma file
2. Figma -> Roblox mapping
3. Route A: Claude with the Figma MCP server
4. Route B: community plugins
5. Images and fonts

## 1. Setting up the Figma file
- One top-level frame per ScreenGui, 1920x1080, named exactly like the ScreenGui (`Hud`, `Shop`). Add a phone check frame (e.g. 844x390) for the HUD to see thumb zones and the top bar.
- Mark the unsafe areas on a hidden guide layer: top ~60 px (Roblox top bar at 1080p), bottom-left thumbstick and bottom-right jump zones on the phone frame.
- Layer names = Roblox instance names in PascalCase (`BuyButton`, `CoinsLabel`): controllers find them by name.
- Figma variables (colors, radii, spacing) named like the spec tokens (`Primary`, `Radius`); text styles named like spec fonts (`Heading`, `Body`).
- Buttons and cards as components with variants Default / Focused / Pressed / Disabled, every glow, light and outline on its own white layer; they become state-tag style rules driven by `assets/UiStates.luau` (one state machine for mouse, touch and gamepad, see `assets/examples/components.json`).
- Text sizes: Roblox `TextSize` is the line height, Figma's font size is the letter size, so the same number reads about a sixth smaller in Roblox. Compare a Studio screenshot with the frame side by side and adjust; letter spacing on titles is lost unless set again.

## 2. Figma -> Roblox mapping
| Figma | Roblox |
| --- | --- |
| Frame / group | Frame (BackgroundTransparency 1 if no fill) |
| Auto layout direction, gap | UIListLayout FillDirection, Padding |
| Auto layout padding | UIPadding |
| Auto layout alignment / space between | HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment / HorizontalFlex SpaceBetween |
| Child "Fill container" | UIFlexItem FlexMode Fill |
| "Hug contents" | AutomaticSize |
| Grid of equal cards | UIGridLayout |
| Corner radius | UICorner (UDim offset in px) |
| Stroke (inside/center) | UIStroke ApplyStrokeMode Border, Thickness |
| Text stroke | UIStroke on the TextLabel (Contextual) |
| Linear gradient | UIGradient Color + Rotation (Figma angle -> Rotation, check visually) |
| Layer opacity | BackgroundTransparency / ImageTransparency / CanvasGroup GroupTransparency |
| Drop shadow | not native: offset dark frame or shadow 9-slice image |
| Background blur | not native: translucent darker panel |
| Constraints left/right/center/top/bottom | AnchorPoint + Scale position (see `studio.md` section 3) |
| Image fill / vector art | exported PNG -> ImageLabel |
| Scrolling content | ScrollingFrame + AutomaticCanvasSize |

Position and size: convert pixel boxes to Scale relative to the parent frame, AnchorPoint from the nearest third of the parent (left/center/right, top/middle/bottom), then a `UIAspectRatioConstraint` with w/h for fixed-shape elements (same rule `psd_to_spec.py` uses).

## 3. Route A: Claude with the Figma MCP server
When the Figma MCP tools are connected (tool names start with `mcp__Figma__`), follow the Figma server's own instructions: it requires loading its `figma-use` skill before `use_figma` (and `figma-generate-design` for building screens). Then:
- **Mock styles or screens in Figma**: create a file (`create_new_file`), build one frame per screen in the chosen style using the tokens from `ui-styles.md` (as Figma variables) and the mapping above, and check it with `get_screenshot`. Good for showing 2-3 style options side by side before building in Studio.
- **Read a designer's file**: `get_metadata` (layer tree, positions, sizes), `get_variable_defs` (tokens), `get_screenshot` (visual reference), `download_assets` for image exports. Write `ui-spec.json` from it with the mapping above, export raster parts into `ui/images/`, then run the normal spec -> build -> validate steps.
- Ask before creating or changing files in the user's Figma account.

## 4. Route B: community plugins
Third-party, check each one's latest version, source and issues before relying on it; all output still needs the responsive checklist in `studio.md`.
- **Figma To Roblox** (NoTwistedHere): Figma plugin that exports the selection to an `.rbxmx`, can upload images through the Open Cloud Assets API with an API key (give the key Assets read/write only, restricted to your IP; never share it). Lists unsupported effects and limited gradient support.
- **Figma Importer Assistant** (MiaGobble): paired Figma + Studio plugins, manual/automatic import, scaling tools, image mapping; open source.
- **RoImport**: paired Figma + Studio plugin, imports tagged objects, Auto Layout and rich text (newer, 2026).
- **FigBloxUI**: commercial paired plugins with automatic image upload (2026).
- **Figblox**: generates Roblox UI code (vanilla Luau or Fusion) from Figma.
- **Quick Roblox UI Exporter by Solys**: exports selected assets as organized PNGs in a ZIP (assets only, no layout).

## 5. Images and fonts
- Export only what can't be native (illustrations, icons, textured panels) as PNG @1x at the size it is shown at 1080p (@2x for small icons that must stay crisp), max 1024 px per image.
- 9-slice candidates: export at a small size with clear corners and note the corner insets for `SliceCenter`.
- Use fonts that exist on Roblox (FredokaOne, LuckiestGuy, Bangers, Michroma, Oswald, Nunito, Roboto, PressStart2P... are Google Fonts you can install for Figma; BuilderSans is Roblox's own). A Figma font that Roblox doesn't have will not survive.

## File: references/photoshop.md

# Photoshop -> Roblox

Photoshop has no Roblox exporter, so this skill ships one: `scripts/psd_to_spec.py` reads the PSD (psd-tools), exports each visual layer as a trimmed PNG and writes `ui-spec.json` with positions converted to Roblox Scale/AnchorPoint. Editable text stays text. Research: psd-tools docs, Adobe UXP docs, DevForum workflows, community Photoshop MCP projects (2025-2026).

## Contents
1. Document setup
2. Layer conventions
3. Export and build
4. What doesn't convert
5. Claude driving Photoshop (MCP)

## 1. Document setup
- 1920x1080 px, RGB 8-bit, 72 ppi: the canvas is the reference screen.
- Guides: top ~60 px for the Roblox top bar; on a phone mock, bottom-left thumbstick and bottom-right jump areas. Put guides/notes in a group tagged `#skip`.
- Fonts: use fonts Roblox has (see `studio.md` section 7) so text layers map 1:1; others fall back to BuilderSans (the script prints the mapping).

## 2. Layer conventions
- Top-level group = one ScreenGui (`HUD`, `Shop Menu` -> `Shop_Menu`). Loose top-level layers go into a `Main` ScreenGui.
- Nested group = Frame. Pixel, shape, smart-object and fill layers = ImageLabel with their own PNG. Text layers = TextLabel (font, size, color and alignment read from the layer).
- Tags in layer names (removed from the Roblox name):

| Tag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `#button` | group -> ImageButton (children inside), image -> ImageButton, text -> TextButton |
| `#slice=N` or `#slice=L,T,R,B` | 9-slice image, N px corners stay fixed while it stretches |
| `#list-v=GAP` / `#list-h=GAP` | group children in a UIListLayout, ordered by position |
| `#scroll` | group -> ScrollingFrame |
| `#raster` | export a text layer as an image (logos, heavily styled titles) |
| `#skip` | ignore (guides, notes, mock backgrounds, screenshots of the game) |

- Hidden layers are ignored. Names should be the instance names the code will use (`Buy Button #button` -> `Buy_Button`; better `BuyButton #button`).
- Button states: separate layers/groups per state (`BuyButton`, `BuyButtonPressed #skip` as reference) or, better, white layers (base, edge, glow) + state style rules that tint and light them (`assets/examples/components.json`).
- Glass or frame layers that stretch must be 9-sliced (`#slice=N`): a frame stretched without slices shows a dark band where only the middle got stretched.

## 3. Export and build
```
pip install psd-tools
python3 scripts/psd_to_spec.py design.psd -o ui --name ShopUI
# upload ui/images/*.png (Studio Asset Manager > Bulk Import), put each rbxassetid into "images" in ui/ui-spec.json
python3 scripts/spec_to_luau.py ui/ui-spec.json -o ui/BuildUi.luau
lune run scripts/validate_ui.luau ui/BuildUi.luau ui/ShopUI.rbxmx
```
Then add tokens/styles to the spec if the UI should be themeable, and run `BuildUi.luau` in Studio.

Positions: each element is placed in Scale relative to its parent, anchored to the nearest third of the parent (so top-right stays top-right on phones), with a `UIAspectRatioConstraint` keeping its shape (except 9-slice images and near full-size panels). Text gets `TextScaled` with `UITextSizeConstraint.MaxTextSize` = its Photoshop size.

## 4. What doesn't convert
- Layer styles (drop shadow, bevel, glow, stroke) may not render in the exported PNG: psd-tools is not Photoshop's renderer. For styled layers, convert to a smart object and rasterize (or merge) before export, or tag text with `#raster`. Text strokes are better rebuilt as UIStroke in the spec.
- Blend modes, adjustment layers and masks on groups: flatten what matters into pixel layers.
- Text effects, tracking and multiple styles inside one text layer: only the first style run is read.
- Exact pixel layout on every screen: the output is responsive (Scale), so check it in the Device Emulator and fix anchors where needed.

## 5. Claude driving Photoshop (MCP)
There is no official Adobe MCP server. Community ones exist, e.g. `mikechambers/adb-mcp` (UXP plugin + proxy), `alisaitteke/photoshop-mcp` (ExtendScript via AppleScript/COM), `StarBoze/Photoshop-MCP-Server`. They are third-party code that controls the user's Photoshop: only suggest them, never install them without the user asking. If one is connected, Claude can build the PSD mock following the conventions above, then run the export script on the saved file.

## File: references/studio.md

# Building UI in Roblox Studio

Rules for UI that works on phones, tablets, PC and console, plus how this skill gets the UI into Studio. Sources: create.roblox.com/docs/ui (layouts, flex, styling, on-screen containers, position and size), DevForum (UI styling full release, Jan 2026).

## Contents
1. Getting the UI into Studio
2. ScreenGui setup and safe areas
3. Size, position and scaling
4. Layout
5. Look: corners, strokes, gradients, 9-slice, images
6. Styling system (StyleSheet)
7. Text and fonts
8. Mobile, gamepad and accessibility
9. Motion
10. Checklist

## 1. Getting the UI into Studio
- **Build script** (best): `spec_to_luau.py` output, run with the Studio MCP `execute_luau` tool (call `list_roblox_studios` first and confirm the place) or pasted into the Command Bar. Creates live StyleSheet rules. Re-running keeps the previous version as `<Name>_Backup` (disabled); delete backups when happy.
- **.rbxmx model** from `validate_ui.luau`: drag into Studio, or put it in a Rojo-synced folder (e.g. `"StarterGui": { "$path": "ui/screens" }`). No style rule values inside; tokens are already resolved on the elements.
- After building, check with the Studio MCP `screen_capture` (or a playtest) at desktop and phone sizes in the Device Emulator.
- Code: controllers (from `roblox-luau-codegen`) find elements by name in `PlayerGui`; never rebuild layout in code that designers maintain in Studio.

## 2. ScreenGui setup and safe areas
- `ResetOnSpawn = false` (UI survives respawn), `ZIndexBehavior = Sibling`.
- `ScreenInsets = CoreUISafeInsets` for anything interactive: keeps it clear of the Roblox top bar and notches. `DeviceSafeInsets` for full-bleed visuals that may sit under the top bar. `None` only for backgrounds/vignettes.
- One ScreenGui per independent layer (HUD, menus, popups, loading) so they can be enabled separately; `DisplayOrder` decides which is on top.

## 3. Size, position and scaling
- Position and size in Scale, not Offset, so the UI follows the screen. Offset only for small fixed things (stroke widths, paddings, gaps).
- `AnchorPoint` matching the edge an element belongs to: top-left HUD (0,0), top-right (1,0), bottom-center (0.5,1), centered popups (0.5,0.5). Then a different aspect ratio keeps it in place.
- `UIAspectRatioConstraint` on anything with a fixed shape (icons, cards, buttons, panels). Default AspectType FitWithinMaxSize keeps it inside its Scale box on every screen.
- `UISizeConstraint` to cap panels on huge monitors; `AutomaticSize` for containers that grow with content.
- Never leave an axis at zero (`Size` scale and offset both 0) expecting a constraint to fill it: `UIAspectRatioConstraint` only shrinks an element to fit its box, it never grows a zero axis. `SizeConstraint = RelativeYY` makes the width `X.Scale x parent height` (so square icons in a row: `Size = (1, 0, 1, 0)` + RelativeYY, not `(0, 0, 1, 0)`).
- Lists inside a `ScrollingFrame` with `AutomaticCanvasSize`: give items an Offset height (`UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 120)`, scaled globally with a `UIScale`) or `AutomaticSize = Y`; Scale heights there are relative to the growing canvas. Grids: `UIGridLayout` with a `UIAspectRatioConstraint` child keeps cells square at any width.
- Design reference 1920x1080; check 16:9, 19.5:9 phones (landscape), 4:3 tablets.

## 4. Layout
- `UIListLayout` for rows/columns; `Padding` for gaps, `SortOrder = LayoutOrder`, alignment properties for placement. Flex: `HorizontalFlex` / `VerticalFlex` (Fill, SpaceBetween, SpaceAround, SpaceEvenly), `Wraps` for wrapping rows, `ItemLineAlignment`; a `UIFlexItem` child with `FlexMode` Fill/Grow/Shrink/Custom makes one item flexible.
- `UIGridLayout` for inventories/shops (`CellSize` in Scale + `UIAspectRatioConstraint` on cells); `UIPadding` for inner spacing.
- `ScrollingFrame` with `AutomaticCanvasSize` for long lists; `ScrollBarThickness` 6-8.
- Layouts own their children's position (and size with flex): don't set those by hand on laid-out children.

## 5. Look: corners, strokes, gradients, 9-slice, images
- `UICorner.CornerRadius`: `UDim(0, px)` for fixed rounding, `UDim(1, 0)` for pills/circles.
- `UIStroke`: `ApplyStrokeMode = Border` on frames/buttons, `Contextual` (default) on text for outlines; `LineJoinMode` Round for soft looks.
- `UIGradient`: `Color` (ColorSequence), `Transparency` (NumberSequence), `Rotation` (90 = top to bottom).
- Drop shadows: no native shadow. Use a duplicate dark frame offset a few px behind (hard comic shadow) or a soft shadow 9-slice image.
- 9-slice: `ScaleType = Slice`, `SliceCenter = Rect(left, top, right, bottom)` in source pixels, `SliceScale` to resize the corners. Use for panels, glass, frames and buttons that change size: the corners stay whole and only the middle stretches, so one image fits every size. A frame stretched without slices (or with a wrong SliceCenter) shows as a dark band down the side of every card; `spec_to_luau.py --images ui/images` checks SliceCenter against the PNG.
- Layered components: build a card or button from separate layers (glow outside, glass/base, edge light, item glow, icon, text, gold line) inside a transparent `ImageButton`, each a white image tinted by `ImageColor3`, ZIndex in that order. Children always draw above their parent, so the glow must be a sibling layer behind the base, never a child of it. Light lives on its own layer so states can move it.
- Images: PNG with transparency; keep each image <= 1024 px (memory on phones; uploads accept larger); sprite sheets via `ImageRectOffset`/`ImageRectSize`; pixel art with `ResampleMode = Pixelated`.
- Upload: Studio Asset Manager (Bulk Import) or Creator Hub; new accounts have Asset Privacy on, so images are Restricted and the experience needs permission (automatic when an editor inserts them in Studio). Images pass moderation before players see them.
- `CanvasGroup` for fading or tinting a whole panel at once (costs extra memory; don't use for everything). `ViewportFrame` for 3D item/pet previews.

## 6. Styling system (StyleSheet)
Released for live games in January 2026. The build script creates it from `tokens` and `styles`:
- `StyleSheet` holds tokens as attributes and `StyleRule` children; `StyleLink` (child of a ScreenGui, `StyleSheet` property) applies it; `StyleDerive` inherits another sheet (e.g. a base theme + a seasonal theme).
- Rule `Selector`: `TextButton`, `.Tag`, `#Name`, `ImageLabel#Glow`, states `:Hover` / `:Press` / `:NonInteractable` / `:Idle` (the `Enum.GuiState` names; `:Pressed` does not exist), `::UICorner`, `A > B` (child), `A >> B` (descendant; a space is not a combinator), `A, B` (list); `Priority` breaks ties; `SetProperty` / `SetProperties` set values, `"$Token"` references a token; `SetDefaultPropertyTransition(TweenInfo)` makes the rule's properties tween instead of snapping (spec: `"transition"`).
- Use it for themes (light/dark, seasonal events), button states, and keeping colors consistent. Designers can then edit tokens in Studio's Style Editor.

## 7. Text and fonts
- `FontFace = Font.new("rbxasset://fonts/families/<Family>.json", Enum.FontWeight.X, Enum.FontStyle.Normal)`. Families seen on Roblox: BuilderSans, GothamSSm, SourceSansPro, FredokaOne, LuckiestGuy, Bangers, Creepster, Michroma, Zekton, Jura, TitilliumWeb, Sarpanch, Oswald, Roboto, RobotoCondensed, RobotoMono, Nunito, Ubuntu, Arimo, PressStart2P, SpecialElite, GrenzeGotisch, Fondamento, Merriweather, DenkOne, PatrickHand, Kalam, AmaticSC, IndieFlower, PermanentMarker, JosefinSans. Confirm in the Studio font picker; a wrong family silently falls back.
- `TextScaled = true` + `UITextSizeConstraint` (MinTextSize ~14 on phones, MaxTextSize at the design size) so text fits every screen; or fixed `TextSize` + `AutomaticSize` for paragraphs.
- `RichText` for inline color/bold (`<b>`, `<font color="#FFB21E">`).
- Leave room for translation (German/Portuguese run ~30% longer); never bake text into images unless it is a logo.

## 8. Mobile, gamepad and accessibility
- Thumb zones: bottom-left is the movement thumbstick, bottom-right the jump button; put frequent actions near the right thumb (around the jump button), never under either control.
- Touch targets: big. As a rule of thumb at least ~44-48 px on a phone screen and spaced apart; check in the Device Emulator on the smallest phone.
- Show only what matters during play; open the rest on demand; use ProximityPrompts for context actions instead of permanent buttons.
- Gamepad/console: every button `Selectable`, a sensible `NextSelection*` chain, `GuiService.SelectedObject` set when a menu opens; `Activated` events work for touch, mouse and gamepad.
- Contrast: body text >= 4.5:1 against its background; don't rely on color alone (rarity also needs a label/icon).
- Settings: music/SFX volume, reduced motion/flashing, UI scale (`UIScale` on a root frame).

## 9. Motion
- One table of numbers for the whole UI (spec `motion`): focus grows to 1.04, press drops to 0.98, hover 0.12 s, press 0.08 s, windows open in 0.3 s with cards 0.05 s apart. Every component uses the same numbers, so the UI feels like one game; style rules reference them as `$MotionHoverScale` etc. and tween with `"transition"`.
- States: Default, Focused (mouse over or gamepad selection), Pressed (mouse, finger or gamepad A held), Disabled. `assets/UiStates.luau` sets them as tags (`StateFocused`, `StatePressed`, `StateDisabled`) the same way for every input; touch never hovers. Picking something means more light (glow, brighter edge), not a new color.
- Pop-in: `UiStates:open(container)` scales components 0.9 -> 1 with `Enum.EasingStyle.Back`, Out, one after another; fade with `GroupTransparency` on CanvasGroups.
- Respect the reduced-motion setting (`UiStates.bind(gui, { reducedMotion = true })`): no breathing glow, no pop-in; states still change.

## 10. Checklist
1. Everything interactive inside `CoreUISafeInsets`; nothing under thumbstick/jump.
2. Scale-based layout + AnchorPoints + aspect constraints; tested at 16:9, 19.5:9, 4:3 in the emulator.
3. Text readable at the smallest phone (>= 14 px), contrast OK, translations fit.
4. Every button has focused/pressed/disabled feedback that works with mouse, touch (no hover) and gamepad selection (the glow replaces the default selection box).
5. Images uploaded, approved, permitted for the experience; no `rbxassetid://0` left.
6. Names match what the controllers expect; no leftover `_Backup` ScreenGuis.
7. One style used consistently (tokens), reward/hype moments stand out from routine UI.

## File: references/ui-spec.md

# ui-spec format

One JSON file describes the UI; every pipeline (Studio, Figma, Photoshop) ends in it. `scripts/spec_to_luau.py` turns it into a build script, `scripts/validate_ui.luau` checks it against Roblox's real class/property database. Full examples: `assets/examples/style-tile-bubbly.json` (a style tile) and `assets/examples/components.json` (layered `ItemCard` and `Button` in all four states, with `motion`, transitions, 9-slice and the layer images in `assets/examples/images/`).

## Top level
```json
{
  "name": "FoodTruckUI",            // identifier; also the StyleSheet name
  "reference": [1920, 1080],        // design resolution (informational)
  "parent": "StarterGui",           // optional service to build into
  "tokens": { "Primary": { "color": "#FFB21E" }, "Radius": { "udim": [0, 16] } },
  "fonts": { "Heading": { "family": "FredokaOne", "weight": "Regular" } },
  "images": { "coin": "rbxassetid://0" },
  "motion": { "hoverScale": 1.04, "pressScale": 0.98, "hoverTime": 0.12 },
  "styles": [ { "selector": "TextButton:Hover", "props": { "BackgroundColor3": { "token": "PrimaryHover" } },
                "transition": { "time": { "token": "MotionHoverTime" }, "easing": "Quad", "direction": "Out" } } ],
  "screens": [ { "class": "ScreenGui", "name": "Hud", "props": {}, "children": [] } ]
}
```
(Comments above are for reading only; JSON has none.)

## Nodes
`{ "class": "Frame", "name": "Panel", "props": {...}, "children": [...], "tags": ["Card"], "attributes": {...} }`
- `class`: any Roblox class (Frame, TextLabel, TextButton, ImageLabel, ImageButton, ScrollingFrame, CanvasGroup, ViewportFrame, UICorner, UIStroke, UIGradient, UIPadding, UIListLayout, UIGridLayout, UIFlexItem, UIAspectRatioConstraint, UISizeConstraint, UITextSizeConstraint, UIScale...).
- `name`: becomes `Instance.Name`. Names are the contract with the code: controllers find elements by name, so use stable PascalCase names (`BuyButton`, `CoinsLabel`).
- `tags`: CollectionService tags; style selectors `.Tag` match them.
- Screens must be ScreenGui / SurfaceGui / BillboardGui. Recommended ScreenGui props: `ResetOnSpawn: false`, `ZIndexBehavior: Sibling`, `ScreenInsets: CoreUISafeInsets`.

## Values
Plain numbers, booleans and strings are used as-is. Everything else is a one-key object:

| Encoding | Example | Roblox type |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `udim2` | `{ "udim2": [0.5, 0, 0.1, 0] }` | UDim2 (xScale, xOffset, yScale, yOffset) |
| `udim` | `{ "udim": [0, 12] }` | UDim |
| `vector2` | `{ "vector2": [0.5, 0.5] }` | Vector2 |
| `rect` | `{ "rect": [24, 24, 104, 104] }` | Rect (SliceCenter) |
| `color` | `{ "color": "#FFB21E" }` | Color3 |
| `token` | `{ "token": "Primary" }` | the token's value |
| `enum` | `{ "enum": "ScaleType.Slice" }` | EnumItem |
| `font` | `{ "font": "Heading" }` or `{ "font": { "family": "LuckiestGuy", "weight": "Bold" } }` | Font (`rbxasset://fonts/families/<family>.json`) |
| `image` | `{ "image": "coin" }` | the content ID from `images` |
| `colorseq` | `{ "colorseq": [[0, "#FFFFFF"], [1, "#000000"]] }` | ColorSequence |
| `numseq` | `{ "numseq": [[0, 0], [1, 0.6]] }` | NumberSequence |

## Tokens and styles
- Tokens are the design system: colors, radii, gaps. Element props reference them with `{ "token": "Name" }`; the builder resolves them, so the UI looks right even without styles.
- The builder also creates `ReplicatedStorage.UIStyles.<name>` (a StyleSheet holding the tokens as attributes) and a `StyleLink` in every ScreenGui. `styles` rules keep token references live (`"$Primary"`), so changing a token in the Style Editor restyles the whole UI.
- Selectors (Roblox UI styling, released Jan 2026): `TextButton` (class), `.Danger` (tag), `#BuyButton` (name), `ImageLabel#Glow` (class + name), `TextButton:Hover` / `:Press` / `:NonInteractable` (state, the `Enum.GuiState` names), `TextButton::UICorner` (the button's UICorner child), `.Panel > TextButton` (direct child), `.Panel >> TextLabel` (any descendant), `A, B` (list). `spec_to_luau.py` rejects unknown states (`:Pressed`, `:Selected`) and spaces used as combinators.
- Style rules override properties set on elements, so put shared looks in rules and one-offs in props.
- `transition` on a rule: its properties tween to the new values (`StyleRule:SetDefaultPropertyTransition`); `time` is seconds or a token, `easing` an `Enum.EasingStyle` name, `direction` In/Out/InOut.

## Motion
`motion` holds the shared animation numbers; each becomes a token `Motion<Key>` (`hoverScale` -> `$MotionHoverScale`) on the StyleSheet, usable in props, rules and transitions, and read by `assets/UiStates.luau` at runtime. Missing keys get the defaults; values outside the range are spec errors.

| Key | Default | Range | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hoverScale` / `pressScale` | 1.04 / 0.98 | 1-1.15 / 0.85-1 | `UIScale.Scale` when focused / pressed |
| `hoverTime` / `pressTime` | 0.12 / 0.08 | s | transitions into focused / pressed |
| `openTime` / `stagger` | 0.3 / 0.05 | s | window pop-in, delay between components |
| `glowIdle` / `glowFocused` / `glowPressed` | 1 / 0.35 / 0.15 | 0-1 | glow layer `ImageTransparency` per state |
| `disabledTransparency` | 0.5 | 0-0.9 | text and icon when disabled |
| `breathe` | 1.6 | 0-5 s | glow swell period while focused (0 = off) |

## Components and states
Interactive components (`assets/examples/components.json`): a transparent `ImageButton` tagged `Button` or `ItemCard` holding white layers (`Glow`, `Base`/`Glass`, `Edge`, `ItemGlow`, `Icon`, labels), each tinted with `ImageColor3`, 9-sliced where it stretches. `assets/UiStates.luau` (client) tags each component `StateFocused`, `StatePressed` or `StateDisabled` (attribute `Disabled = true`) from mouse, touch and gamepad input, and style rules like `.StateFocused > ImageLabel#Glow` or `.StatePressed > UIScale` give each state its look. A state gallery in the spec carries the tags statically, so the build, the preview and the game show the same states.

## Commands
```
python3 scripts/spec_to_luau.py ui/ui-spec.json -o ui/BuildUi.luau --images ui/images  # structure, references, selectors, motion, 9-slice
lune run scripts/validate_ui.luau ui/BuildUi.luau ui/FoodTruckUI.rbxmx  # property/type/enum checks + model file
```
Run `BuildUi.luau` in Studio (Command Bar, or the Studio MCP `execute_luau` tool) to build into StarterGui; an existing ScreenGui with the same name is renamed `<Name>_Backup` and disabled. The `.rbxmx` can be dragged into Studio or synced by Rojo, but it contains no style rule values (Lune can't write them); elements still carry their resolved look.

## File: references/ui-styles.md

# Roblox UI styles

Starting presets for proposing a UI direction. Each gives tokens ready for `ui-spec.json`, fonts available on Roblox (`rbxasset://fonts/families/<Family>.json`; confirm in Studio's font picker), shape language, motion and where it fits. Example games show the direction, not a copy target. Research: Roblox Creator Hub art-style guidance, DevForum, current top games (2024-2026).

## Choosing
- Match genre and audience first (see `roblox-game-idea-validator` genre notes), then the game's world art: UI that fights the 3D style looks cheap.
- Propose 2-3 that fit, recommend one, say why in one line each. Mixing two styles is fine only as "base + accent" (e.g. Clean Minimal menus with Bubbly reward popups).
- Every style must still pass the mobile/readability checklist in `studio.md`.

## Contents
1. Bubbly Cartoon
2. Clean Minimal
3. Glass Modern
4. Anime / Gacha
5. Sci-fi Neon HUD
6. Horror / Grunge
7. Pixel Retro
8. Cozy Pastel
9. Competitive Minimal HUD
10. Fantasy Medieval
11. Comic Meme Pop

---

## 1. Bubbly Cartoon
Simulators, tycoons, obbies, pet/collect games, younger audience. Examples: Pet Simulator 99, Adopt Me!, most front-page simulators.
- Tokens: Primary `#FFB21E`, PrimaryHover `#FFC94D`, Secondary `#3FA9F5`, Success `#4CD964`, Danger `#FF4D5E`, Surface `#2B2F77`, SurfaceLight `#4A50B5`, Outline `#14163D`, Text `#FFFFFF`.
- Fonts: headings FredokaOne or LuckiestGuy; numbers/body BuilderSans Bold.
- Shape: big radius (16-24 px or pill `udim [1,0]`), thick dark UIStroke (4-6 px) on panels AND text, vertical UIGradient lighter on top, chunky buttons ~2x text height.
- Icons: glossy, outlined, slightly tilted; currency icons next to every number.
- Motion: pop-in scale 0.8 -> 1 with Back Out 0.2 s; button press UIScale 0.92; reward bursts with particles/confetti; number count-up tweens.
- Watch: too many colors fighting; outline on everything makes text noisy at small sizes (drop text stroke below ~18 px).

## 2. Clean Minimal
RPG menus, social/utility games, older audience, settings-heavy games. Example: Roblox's own Spellbound RPG UI tutorial.
- Tokens: Primary `#3D7BFF`, Surface `#FFFFFF` (light) or `#1C1F26` (dark), SurfaceAlt `#F2F4F7` / `#262A33`, Border `#D5DAE1` / `#343A46`, Text `#111827` / `#F3F4F6`, TextMuted `#6B7280` / `#9CA3AF`.
- Fonts: BuilderSans (Regular/Bold), GothamSSm.
- Shape: radius 8-12, 1 px stroke or none, generous padding (16-24), flat fills, no gradients.
- Icons: line icons, single color.
- Motion: 0.15-0.2 s Quad Out fades and 8-12 px slides; nothing bounces.
- Watch: can feel empty on Roblox; add one accent color and real hierarchy.

## 3. Glass Modern
Showcase/hangout, lifestyle, modern city RP, premium-feel menus.
- Tokens: Surface `#0E1220` at 0.35-0.5 BackgroundTransparency, Border `#FFFFFF` at 0.8 transparency, Accent `#7C5CFF`, Accent2 `#22D3EE`, Text `#FFFFFF`, TextMuted `#B8C0D9`.
- Fonts: BuilderSans, GothamSSm, Montserrat-like headings with GothamSSm Bold.
- Shape: radius 14-20, 1-2 px light stroke, subtle white-to-transparent UIGradient on Transparency; Roblox UI has no background blur, so fake it with darker translucent panels (or a blurred screenshot image behind menus).
- Motion: smooth 0.25 s Sine fades; CanvasGroup GroupTransparency for whole-panel fades.
- Watch: text contrast over busy 3D scenes; test outdoors at noon and at night.

## 4. Anime / Gacha
Tower defense, battlegrounds, unit collection, summon banners. Examples: Anime Defenders, Anime Adventures.
- Tokens: Surface `#121428`, Panel `#1E2245`, Gold `#FFC93C`, rarity Common `#B0B7C3`, Rare `#3FA9F5`, Epic `#A855F7`, Legendary `#FFB21E`, Mythic `#FF3D7F`, Text `#FFFFFF`.
- Fonts: headings Sarpanch, Bangers or LuckiestGuy (all caps); body BuilderSans Bold.
- Shape: angled/cut-corner frames (9-slice images), metallic gold strokes, rarity-colored glows (UIStroke + UIGradient), character art cards.
- Motion: summon reveals with flash, card flip, rarity color sweep; keep routine menus fast.
- Watch: rarity colors must be learnable and consistent everywhere; paid random items need odds displayed.

## 5. Sci-fi Neon HUD
Space, cyberpunk, futuristic shooters/racers. Pairs with the map builder's NEON preset.
- Tokens: Background `#070B14`, Panel `#0D1526` at 0.2 transparency, Cyan `#23E5F3`, Magenta `#F046C7`, Violet `#865BFF`, Amber `#FFB347`, Text `#E6F7FF`.
- Fonts: Michroma or Zekton for headings, Jura or TitilliumWeb for body, RobotoMono for numbers.
- Shape: square or 2-4 px radius, thin 1-2 px glowing strokes, corner brackets, scanline/grid images at low opacity.
- Motion: quick 0.1 s scans, flicker-in once, pulsing only for warnings.
- Watch: neon text on dark at small sizes blurs; keep body text plain light gray.

## 6. Horror / Grunge
Horror, survival, mystery. Examples: DOORS, The Mimic.
- Tokens: Background `#0B0B0C`, Panel `#18171A` at 0.15 transparency, Paper `#D8D2C4`, Blood `#8E1B1B`, Muted `#7A746A`, Text `#E8E2D5`.
- Fonts: headings Creepster (sparingly), SpecialElite or GrenzeGotisch; instructions in BuilderSans.
- Shape: torn/scratched 9-slice panels, no bright gradients, minimal HUD (hide when not needed).
- Motion: slow 0.4-0.6 s fades, rare flicker, heartbeat pulse on danger; offer reduced flashing.
- Watch: atmosphere must not hide interaction prompts and health; test on low-brightness phones.

## 7. Pixel Retro
Arcade, retro obbies, 8/16-bit themed games.
- Tokens: a fixed 8-16 color palette, e.g. Black `#1A1C2C`, Purple `#5D275D`, Red `#B13E53`, Orange `#EF7D57`, Yellow `#FFCD75`, Green `#38B764`, Blue `#3B5DC9`, White `#F4F4F4`.
- Fonts: PressStart2P for short labels and numbers; a readable second font (BuilderSans) for long text.
- Shape: square corners, 2-4 px hard borders, pixel-art images with `ResampleMode = Pixelated` and integer scaling.
- Motion: stepped movement (tween in 2-4 steps), quick flashes, no smooth easing.
- Watch: PressStart2P is wide and hard to read; keep it short and large.

## 8. Cozy Pastel
Roleplay, farming/garden, decorating, cafe/pet care, younger and casual audience. Examples: Adopt Me!, Berry Avenue, garden-style games.
- Tokens: Cream `#FFF7EC`, Peach `#FFC8A2`, Mint `#B8E6C9`, Sky `#BFE3FF`, Lavender `#D9C8FF`, Rose `#FFB3C7`, Brown `#6B4E3D` (text/outline), Accent `#FF8FA3`.
- Fonts: FredokaOne or PatrickHand/Kalam for headings, Nunito or BuilderSans for body.
- Shape: radius 16-28, soft 2-3 px brown strokes, light gradients, sticker-like icons with white outline.
- Motion: gentle bounce 0.25 s, floating idle on reward items.
- Watch: pastel on pastel kills contrast; text in dark brown, not white.

## 9. Competitive Minimal HUD
Shooters, fighting, racing, anything where reaction time matters. Examples: RIVALS, Arsenal.
- Tokens: Panel `#000000` at 0.5-0.6 transparency, Text `#FFFFFF`, Ally `#3FA9F5`, Enemy `#FF4D5E`, Warning `#FFC93C`, Health `#4CD964`.
- Fonts: Oswald or RobotoCondensed for numbers, BuilderSans for labels.
- Shape: small radius 4-6, no strokes, compact; everything at the edges, center of the screen clear except crosshair.
- Motion: instant feedback (hit markers, damage numbers), no menu animations during combat.
- Watch: on phones keep fire/ability buttons in the right-thumb zone and huge.

## 10. Fantasy Medieval
RPG, adventure, dungeon, kingdom builders.
- Tokens: Parchment `#E9D8A6`, Wood `#5C3A21`, Iron `#4A4E57`, Gold `#D4A23C`, Crimson `#9B2226`, Ink `#2B1B10`.
- Fonts: Fondamento or Merriweather headings, GrenzeGotisch for titles only, BuilderSans for numbers.
- Shape: parchment and wood 9-slice panels, gold trim strokes, ornate corners as images, ribbons for titles.
- Motion: scroll unroll, page turn, weighty 0.3 s Quad Out.
- Watch: heavy textures make phone UIs muddy; keep inventory grids plain.

## 11. Comic Meme Pop
Meme/brainrot, chaotic party games, troll obbies, short-trend games.
- Tokens: Yellow `#FFE600`, Pink `#FF4FA3`, Cyan `#00E0FF`, Black `#111111`, White `#FFFFFF`, Red `#FF3B30`.
- Fonts: Bangers or LuckiestGuy, all caps.
- Shape: thick black strokes (5-8 px), offset hard shadows (duplicate frame offset 6 px down-right in black), halftone/burst images, tilted labels (Rotation -3..3).
- Motion: shake on rewards, punchy scale 1.2 -> 1, comic "POW" bursts.
- Watch: readability collapses fast; keep core HUD calmer than the popups.
